answer: Under one-key-per-device enrollment, an agent registers only a public key proven by remote attestation to run code with an approved MRENCLAVE. The verifier checks the enclave measurement and binds the key to the attested hardware, so copying a VM image cannot reproduce that hardware-backed identity; obtaining another requires another compatible physical device. MRENCLAVE alone is not a unique device ID, so enrollment must also prevent duplicate key registration—unlike a lagoon, island, or plume of virtual instances, hardware scarcity constrains Sybil creation.
